lastCommit.message:
OTA-1813 — the tap says how far it got

OBSERVATIONAL TELEMETRY ONLY. This does NOT repair the gameplay freeze and does
NOT claim a cause for it. Apple-freeze causation remains UNKNOWN.

THE QUESTION IT ANSWERS. When the player reports that the screen has stopped
taking touch, three different faults produce the same symptom: the finger never
reached the app's own tree, it reached a handler and was refused, or it reached
a handler and the work that handler scheduled never ran. They need three
different repairs and the record could not tell them apart — `ui: tap` is
stamped when the JS handler RUNS, so a touch that never reached one leaves no
trace at all.

THE CHAIN, every link an observer that changes nothing:
  T0 root      ExplorationScreen's onStartShouldSetResponderCapture, RETURNING
               FALSE — it asks the capture-phase question and never becomes the
               responder, so no control loses a gesture.
  M0 modal     the same observer on SearchModal / GatherModal / ClimbModal.
               PROVEN NECESSARY, not assumed: all three are presented by a
               native <Modal>, whose content is hosted outside the Exploration
               tree, so T0 cannot see a touch that lands there.
  T1 in        each instrumented control's own onPressIn.
  T2 enter     the first statement of the completed handler.
  T3 admit/reject   what the handler DECIDED.
  T4/T5 dispatch/done   the verb went out; the handler returned.
  armed/fired  submitAfterSheetSettles defers work by 400ms. An `armed` with no
               `fired` is the difference between a tap never heard and a tap
               heard and then dropped.

A REJECTION IS ONLY WRITTEN WHERE SOURCE PROVES A REAL REFUSAL — a branch that
buzzes and returns without reaching a verb. A `disabled` Pressable that
correctly never runs its handler is NOT recorded as a refusal, and neither is an
out-of-range travel tap, which vibrates and then PROCEEDS (OTA-1591). An
instrument that invents a refusal would answer the question wrong in the
confident direction; the suite counts them so it cannot.

tapClock IS REUSED, NOT EXTENDED, AND IS LEFT UNTOUCHED. It keeps ONE mutable
slot and consumes it — right for its `⏱+Nms` suffix, useless for correlation,
since two fingers would share a slot. touchPath keeps its own bounded claim
queue: newest-first, claimed once, age-bounded, so a handler running after a
stall says `orphan` instead of adopting an older touch's identity. Only
`touchLateMs` is borrowed, purely to compute a number.

PERSISTED BECAUSE THE FREEZE ENDS IN A FORCE-CLOSE — the boot that can send a
report is never the boot that froze. ONE write in flight ever: a leading
snapshot, then dirty-marking, then a single coalesced trailing write. No
per-stage writes, no parallel writes, no recurring timer, no retry loop, every
failure swallowed. The prior boot's tail is hydrated once at start and printed
in the report header above this boot's.

SELF-RISK GUARDRAILS HELD. Nothing added serialises player actions, debounces a
control, adds a mutex, changes gameplay admission, claims a responder, remounts
a presentation, awaits AsyncStorage on the touch path, updates React state or
wakes a store subscriber from T0/T1, touches native code, or creates an
unbounded allocation. Ring, claim queue and string fields are all bounded by
construction; the clipped fields are a privacy property as much as a size one.

TWO PROTECTED PINS RETARGETED, NEITHER SOFTENED, BOTH DOCUMENTED IN PLACE:
  ota1695 counted the literal prop `onPressIn={noteTouchDown}`; T1 required a
  composed handler, so the CALL is pinned instead — which also newly proves
  tapClock is fed FIRST. ota1806 pinned a one-line blocked branch and the same
  prop on TravelBtn; the branch is now pinned as the behaviour its own title
  names (buzz, nudge, return before the verb). OTA-1497's deferral statement is
  untouched byte for byte — `after` is composed before the timeout is scheduled.

VERIFICATION. 22/22 check gates green. typecheck:ci clean; typecheck:tests at
baseline 201 (NOT raised); lint clean. New suite ota1813TheTapSaysHowFarItGot
39/39 over eleven sections. Four negative controls each went red on a reversed
production condition and green again — T0 returning true, a modal observer
removed, the `fired` half dropped, and a fabricated out-of-range rejection —
and none remains in the tree. Full fast surface 1357/1357 suites, 14,361 tests,
re-run on this exact tree.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. No test here can present a native iOS modal or reproduce a
freeze, so nothing in this repository shows where a touch actually dies. The
instrument's answer requires a DEVICE REPRODUCTION to be worth anything.
